tasks.short: Oversee facility purchase, planning, design, construction and upkeep.

steps.what: See the recreation facilities and areas that need upkeep.
inputs: the recreation facilities and areas
outputs: what the worker saw that needs upkeep

steps.what: Read the purchase and upkeep notes for those recreation facilities.
inputs: what the worker saw that needs upkeep
upkeep card when the facilities keeper has written one
outputs: the purchase and upkeep notes that apply

steps.what: Decide the planning, design and construction those facilities need, and record that decision.
inputs: what the worker saw that needs upkeep
the purchase and upkeep notes that apply
outputs: the recorded planning, design and construction decision

steps.what: Oversee the purchase and the upkeep while that work is done.
inputs: the recorded planning, design and construction decision
outputs: the purchase and upkeep the worker oversaw

tasks.design: The facilities keeper keeps a paper upkeep card: area, what is due, the supplier for a routine purchase, and the last date. The recreation worker sees the facilities, reads that card or the posted notice when a row is missing, decides the planning, design and construction, and oversees the purchase and the upkeep in person. Nothing sends a purchase, raises an alert, or fills a form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase and upkeep notes sat in old folders, so each round started as a search. The condition of an area is visible only by walking it.
tasks.enabler_now: The facilities keeper already knows the supplier and the last date. Writing them on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what is worn, deciding design and construction, and overseeing the purchase and the upkeep stay with the worker.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an area needs design and construction or only upkeep, from what they can see on site.
tasks.altitude: Finding the supplier and the last date is shorter when the card is current. The worker still walks the site, still decides, and still oversees the purchase and the upkeep.

reach.task: Keep the upkeep card for each recreation area
reach.learn: To name the area, what is due, the supplier, and the last date, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Overseeing facility purchase, planning, design, construction and upkeep is a site visit, a decision, and watching the work. A card shortens finding the supplier and the last date. It does not see the area or oversee the work. Model knowledge.
An app that time-stamps each upkeep check can monitor how the worker spends the visit. National works-council rules require consent for that. This task adds no such app.

assumptions: The boundary is one recreation area and one round of purchase, planning, design, construction or upkeep. Seeing, deciding and overseeing each keep their full time.

Upkeep card fields are area, what is due, supplier for a routine purchase, and last date. The producer is the facilities keeper, when a job finishes or a supplier changes. If a row is missing or stale, the worker reads the posted notice inside the lookup. The quantity and the condition come from what the worker sees in s1, not from the card.
The card does not send a purchase, raise an alert, or fill a form. The worker tells people what to do while overseeing. That talk is the oversee step, not a system action.
Card upkeep is the facilities keeper's 1.5 hours per 100 worker hours on this task. The worker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a buyer, not the recreation worker, places the purchase, and how much of the oversee step is only watching.
Which construction decisions the organisation reserves for a project lead.
research_questions: Of the facility rounds in a month, how many are answered by a current upkeep card, and how many change because of what the worker sees on site?

incremental.description: The recreation worker adds no recurring chore. Seeing, deciding and overseeing stay in the steps above.
The facilities keeper writes the upkeep card by hand when a job finishes or a supplier changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the upkeep card has no row, the worker reads the posted notice inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Walking the site, the planning decision, and overseeing the purchase and upkeep never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage participants' own activities and leadership in discussion.

steps.what: Read which activities this group may develop before the discussion.
inputs: this group
activity card when the programme lead has written one
outputs: the activities this group may develop

steps.what: Encourage participants through group discussions to develop their own activities and leadership skills.
inputs: the activities this group may develop
the participants in the discussion
outputs: the encouragement given in that group discussion

tasks.design: The programme lead keeps a paper activity card: group, activity, and who may lead it. The recreation worker reads that card, or the posted programme when a row is missing, then encourages the participants in the group discussion. The discussion stays in the room. Nothing sends a prompt, raises an alert, or fills a form.
tasks.previous_blocker: The list of activities a group may lead sat in a folder, so the worker looked it up before the discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: The programme lead already holds that list. Writing the current rows on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Encouraging this group, and hearing who is ready to lead, stays in the discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing who hangs back and who is ready to lead an activity, in this discussion.
tasks.altitude: Finding which activities the group may lead is shorter when the card is current. The worker still leads the discussion and still encourages the participants.

reach.task: Keep the activity card for each group
reach.learn: To name the group, the activity, and who may lead it, and to remove an activity the programme no longer offers

evidence.claim: Encouraging participants to develop activities and leadership skills happens in a group discussion. A card can list which activities the group may lead. It does not encourage anyone. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one group and one discussion. Encouraging the participants keeps its full time.

Activity card fields are group, activity, and who may lead it. The producer is the programme lead, when the programme changes. If a row is missing, the worker reads the posted programme inside the lookup.
The card does not speak in the discussion, send a prompt, raise an alert, or fill a form. The worker does not score the participants.
Card upkeep is the programme lead's 1 hour per 100 worker hours on this task. The worker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the programme lead and the recreation worker are the same person on a small site.
research_questions: How often does the discussion follow the activity card, and how often does a participant propose an activity the card does not list?

incremental.description: The recreation worker adds no recurring chore. The discussion stays the bulk of the task.
The programme lead writes the activity card by hand when the programme changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the activity card has no row, the worker reads the posted programme inside the lookup, so that step often stays long. The group discussion never shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet partners to plan balanced recreational programs.

steps.what: Read the notes on participants and community organizations before the meeting.
inputs: the meeting
partner card when the programme lead has written one
outputs: the participant and organization notes for this meeting

steps.what: Meet and collaborate with agency personnel, community organizations and other professional personnel.
inputs: the participant and organization notes for this meeting
the people in the meeting
outputs: what the meeting agreed for the participants

steps.what: Record the balanced recreational programs agreed for those participants.
inputs: what the meeting agreed for the participants
outputs: the meeting note of the balanced recreational programs

tasks.design: The programme lead keeps a paper partner card: participant group, need, organization, and contact. The recreation worker reads that card, or the last meeting note when a row is missing, then meets the agency, community and other professional personnel and writes the balanced programs they agreed. The meeting stays in the room. Nothing sends an invite, raises an alert, or fills a form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contacts and participant needs sat in old meeting notes, so each collaboration started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: The programme lead already knows the organizations. Writing the current rows on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Collaborating in the meeting, and writing a balanced program the group can actually run, stay with the worker.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing what participants need against what the organizations in the room can offer.
tasks.altitude: Finding the organization and the contact is shorter when the card is current. The worker still meets the partners and still writes the programs they agreed.

reach.task: Keep the partner card for community organizations
reach.learn: To name the participant group, the need, the organization, and the contact, and to drop a contact who has left

evidence.claim: Planning balanced recreational programs with agency and community personnel is a meeting and a note of what was agreed. A card shortens finding the contact. It does not hold the meeting. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one meeting about one set of participants. The meeting and the handwritten note each keep their full time.

Partner card fields are participant group, need, organization, and contact. The producer is the programme lead, when an organization changes. If a row is missing, the worker reads the last meeting note inside the lookup.
The card does not send an invite, raise an alert, or fill a form. The worker writes the meeting note by hand in s3.
Card upkeep is the programme lead's 1.5 hours per 100 worker hours on this task. The worker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How often the meeting is with people outside the organisation, and how often it is only internal staff.
research_questions: How often is the balanced program settled in the meeting, and how often does it wait on a later decision by someone who was not there?

incremental.description: The recreation worker adds no recurring chore. Meeting and writing the note stay in the steps above.
The programme lead writes the partner card by hand when an organization or contact changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the partner card has no row, the worker reads the last meeting note inside the lookup, so much of that step returns. The meeting and the handwritten program note never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide entertainment and set up decorations and equipment.

steps.what: Read which decorations and equipment this entertainment needs.
inputs: this entertainment
setup card when the events lead has written one
outputs: the decorations and equipment this entertainment needs

steps.what: Provide for that entertainment with the people it is for.
inputs: the decorations and equipment this entertainment needs
the people the entertainment is for

steps.what: Set up the related decorations and equipment for that entertainment.
inputs: the decorations and equipment this entertainment needs
the room
outputs: the decorations and equipment set up

tasks.design: The events lead keeps a paper setup card: entertainment, decoration, equipment, and where it is stored. The recreation worker reads that card, or the event note when a row is missing, then provides the entertainment and sets up the decorations and equipment by hand. Nothing sends a list, raises an alert, or fills a form.
tasks.previous_blocker: What to put out for an entertainment sat on an event note in a folder, so each setup started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: The events lead already knows the store place. Writing it on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Providing the entertainment, and putting the decorations and equipment in place, stay physical and in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether the room as set up actually works for the people who will use it.
tasks.altitude: Finding where the decorations and equipment are stored is shorter when the card is current. The worker still provides the entertainment and still sets up the room.

reach.task: Keep the setup card for each entertainment
reach.learn: To name the entertainment, the decoration, the equipment, and the store place, and to change a row when the store place moves

evidence.claim: Providing entertainment and setting up decorations and equipment is done in the room. A card can name the item and the store place. It does not put anything out or host the entertainment. Model knowledge.
An app that time-stamps each item set out can monitor how the worker spends the setup. National works-council rules require consent for that. This task adds no such app.

assumptions: The boundary is one entertainment in one room. Providing it and setting it up each keep their full time.

Setup card fields are entertainment, decoration, equipment, and store place. The producer is the events lead, when the store place or the list changes. If a row is missing, the worker reads the event note inside the lookup.
The card does not send a list, raise an alert, or fill a form. The worker carries and places the items. That work is s3, not a system action.
Card upkeep is the events lead's 1 hour per 100 worker hours on this task. The worker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the events lead and the recreation worker are the same person on a small site.
Which entertainments bring in an outside performer the worker only sets up for.
research_questions: How often is the decoration list stable enough for a card, and how often does the room force a change the card does not show?

incremental.description: The recreation worker adds no recurring chore. Providing the entertainment and setting up stay in the steps above.
The events lead writes the setup card by hand when the list or the store place changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the setup card has no row, the worker reads the event note inside the lookup, so that step often stays long. Providing the entertainment and setting up the room never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation worker still walks the facilities, decides planning and construction, oversees purchase and upkeep, encourages the group, meets the partners, and sets up entertainment. A current card only shortens finding a supplier, an activity, a contact, or a store place.
reach: A facilities keeper learns to name the area, what is due, the supplier, and the last date before the worker oversees purchase and upkeep.
A programme lead learns to name the group, the activity, and who may lead it before a discussion, and the organization and contact before a partner meeting.
An events lead learns to name the entertainment, the decoration, the equipment, and the store place before the room is set up.
skills_to_grow: Open the posted notice, the posted programme, the last meeting note, or the event note when the card has no row.
Decide planning and construction from what they saw on site, not from the card alone.
Keep the group discussion, the partner meeting, and the entertainment in the room, and do not score participants.
role.ambitious_version: The worker still oversees, encourages, meets, and sets up. The cards do not oversee, encourage, meet, or set up.
